t.15.1: A person of pure understanding reaches fulfilment through instruction given in any manner whatever, while another, though seeking to know throughout his whole life, remains bewildered about it.
t.15.2: Liberation is the loss of taste for sense-objects; bondage is the relish for sense-objects. This much alone is true knowledge; now do as you wish.
t.15.4: You are not the body, nor is the body yours; you are neither the enjoyer nor the doer. You are of the nature of pure consciousness, ever the witness; free of all dependence, wander happily.
t.15.3: This knowledge of the truth makes an eloquent, wise and highly energetic person mute, dull and inactive; therefore it is shunned by those who crave enjoyment.
t.15.5: Attachment and aversion are properties of the mind, and the mind is never yours. You are free of all mental constructs, consciousness itself, unchanging; move about happily.
t.15.6: Having known the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self, be free from ego and free from the sense of 'mine,' and be happy.
t.15.7: That in which this universe shimmers forth like waves upon the ocean, that you yourself are, there is no doubt. O embodiment of consciousness, be free from fever.
t.15.8: Have faith, my child, have faith; do not be deluded about this, my dear. You are the Self, the Lord, whose very nature is knowledge, beyond nature.
t.15.9: The body, enveloped by the guṇas, remains, comes, and goes; the Self neither goes nor comes. Why, then, do you grieve for it?
t.15.10: Let the body remain until the end of the kalpa, or let it go this very day. Where is any gain, and where any loss, for you whose form is pure consciousness alone?
t.15.11: In you, the infinite great ocean, let the wave of the universe rise or let it set by its own nature; for you there is neither increase nor loss.
t.15.12: My child, you are pure consciousness alone; this world is not separate from you. Therefore, for whom, how, and where can there be any notion of what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted?
t.15.13: In you, who are one, imperishable, tranquil, the stainless space of consciousness, whence is birth, whence is action, and whence indeed is the sense of 'I'?
t.15.14: Whatever you see, there you alone appear, one only. Do bracelet, armlet and anklet appear as something separate from the gold?
t.15.15: Give up the distinction "This I am, this I am not." Knowing for certain that all is the Self, be free of intention and be happy.
t.15.16: It is from your ignorance alone that the universe exists; in truth you alone are. Apart from you there is no one bound to saṃsāra, nor anyone free from it.
t.15.17: He who is firmly convinced that this universe is mere illusion and nothing at all becomes free of latent desires; being pure radiance of consciousness, he finds peace as though nothing existed.
t.15.18: Be the One alone in the ocean, the One that was, is, and will be. For you there is neither bondage nor liberation; having done all that was to be done, wander happily.
t.15.19: O you who are pure consciousness, do not agitate your mind with resolves and doubts. Become tranquil and abide happily in your own Self, whose very form is bliss.
t.15.20: Give up meditation altogether; hold nothing whatsoever in your heart. You are the Self, already free; what will you accomplish by deliberating?
